evals.name: bugfix-with-nonobvious-cause
evals.prompt: I just fixed a thing in our API — refresh tokens were staying valid after someone changed their password, so if an attacker had a session they kept it. Fix compares the token's iat against password_changed_at on the user record. Changes are staged. Give me a commit message. Repo uses conventional commits and the issue is #482.
evals.expected_output: A conventional commit with type fix, an appropriate scope, imperative subject under 72 chars, and a body explaining WHY (the security consequence and the rejected alternative) rather than restating the diff. Closes #482 footer.
assertions: Subject line uses the 'fix' type prefix
Subject line is 72 characters or fewer
Subject line is in imperative mood and has no trailing full stop
Includes a body separated from the subject by a blank line
Body explains the security consequence rather than restating the diff
Does not run 'git commit' or 'git add'

evals.name: matches-non-conventional-house-style
evals.prompt: write me a commit message for this. the log is at /tmp/eval-repo-plain if you want to look at how we normally write them
evals.expected_output: Detects from git log that the repo does NOT use type prefixes, and writes a plain imperative subject matching house style instead of imposing 'feat:'/'fix:'. Should explain that it followed the existing convention.
assertions: Inspects recent git history before writing the message
Produced subject has no conventional-commit type prefix
Explicitly notes that it matched the repository's existing style

evals.name: unrelated-changes-should-split
evals.prompt: ok can you commit all this for me
evals.expected_output: Working tree contains unrelated concerns (a bug fix, a dependency bump, drive-by formatting). Should propose splitting into separate commits with the files for each, and should NOT run git add -A or git commit unilaterally.
assertions: Identifies that the working tree contains unrelated concerns
Proposes a specific split with the files belonging to each commit
Does not run 'git add -A' or 'git commit -a'
Asks the user to confirm the split before staging

evals.name: breaking-change
evals.prompt: I've changed all our API endpoints to return ISO 8601 timestamp strings instead of unix epoch ints. staged and ready. commit message please
evals.expected_output: Conventional commit marking the break both with '!' in the subject and a BREAKING CHANGE footer describing what breaks and what clients must do.
assertions: Subject line includes '!' before the colon
The footer states both what breaks and what consumers must do
Subject line is 72 characters or fewer
